world.rule: For each held-out Philippine typhoon, the neural network trained on the other Philippine typhoons alone and with every world event; the world events join only when the AUC gain has its 95% interval wholly above zero.
world.verdict: The world events were left out of this build (it was built from the Philippine typhoons only), so the world test did not run.

choice.rule: The neural network is kept unless logistic regression or XGBoost beats it on pooled out-of-fold AUC with a 95% interval wholly above zero; if both do, the higher pooled AUC wins.
choice.verdict: Logistic regression chosen: its AUC gain over the neural network was 0.042 (95% interval 0.033 to 0.050), wholly above zero.

details.better_than_noah: AUC gain over UP NOAH's map alone 0.090 (95% interval 0.078 to 0.102) on the held-out Philippine typhoons
details.talisay_test: 2 of 2 in Red or Orange (2 needed)

details.tests_seen_last: The training set, the choice and the cut-offs were in the report before any Talisay test record or catalogue point was loaded.

reasons: Red and Orange would cover 100% of the in-range scoring points of Talisay's assessed puroks, more than half.

fallback.note: UP NOAH's landslide map ships because the model failed a gate. Its cut-offs come from the same walk on its classes at the held-out typhoon points, and every purok with a building or road is classed.

limits: The model learned where landslides started after typhoons elsewhere in the Philippines (northern Luzon, Benguet, Maguindanao and Leyte) and is applied to Talisay, whose ground and rain differ.
Terrain comes from a 30 m elevation model, so small road cuts and steep banks are smoothed out.
Geology differs: Cebu's limestone is not the Cordillera's volcanic and sedimentary rock, and the model has no rock or soil map.
The "no landslide" ground was sampled at three points per mapped slide, so a score ranks how prone ground is to sliding; it is not a chance of a landslide.
Few located Talisay landslides exist to test it on, all on the Manipis road side.
Agaton's 23 slides make its held-out typhoon test noisy.
This is not a forecast: it is the same in every month and does not say a landslide is coming.
